days.title: Upper Semois and Ancient History
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Arlon
stops.detail: The Semois rises in Arlon, half a kilometer southeast of the old town, next to the Avenue de Longwy.

stops.name: Chassepierre
stops.detail: Only 42 kilometers further west, at Chassepierre (near Florenville), does the Semois valley gain depth.

stops.name: Cugnon
stops.detail: At Cugnon (belonging to Bertrix) there is a Celtic oppidum from the late La Tène period, which was probably conquered by the Romans during the Gallic Wars.

days.title: Fortresses and the French Border
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Burg von Bouillon
stops.detail: In a narrow loop of the Semois lies the Castle of Bouillon, the ancestral castle of Godfrey of Bouillon, which was expanded into a powerful fortress over the centuries.

stops.name: Bohan
stops.detail: Between Bohan (near Vresse-sur-Semois) and Les Hautes-Rivières, the river crosses the border between Belgium and France and flows into the Meuse after 210 kilometers at Monthermé, whose valley is deeply carved from Charleville-Mézières (15 kilometers south) to Namur (65 kilometers north).

days.title: Natural Beauty of the Meuse Confluence
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Monthermé
stops.detail: The Semois, also known as the Semoy for the section in France (also grammatically feminine), Sesbach (German in Luxembourg), is a river in the southern Ardennes that rises in Arlon in the province of Luxembourg in Belgium and, after a 210-kilometer course, flows from the right into the Meuse at Monthermé, in the Ardennes department of France, with an average water flow of nearly 30 m³/s.

stops.name: Regionalen Naturpark Ardennen
stops.detail: In the French section, the Semois runs through the Ardennes Regional Nature Park.
